questions.question: A crew flies at a level that lies inside the troposphere over the equator but above it over the poles. Which thicknesses of the troposphere account for this?
options: About 8.5 km at the equator and about 16.8 km at the poles
About 16.8 km at the equator and about 8.5 km at the poles
About 16.8 km at the equator and about 11 km at the poles
questions.explain: The troposphere reaches much higher at the equator than at the poles, so the same level can be inside it in one place and above it in the other.

questions.question: A fleet of six aircraft is to be cleared for RVSM. Who must apply for the Airworthiness Approval and for what?
options: The aircraft operator, for the whole fleet at once
The aircraft manufacturer, for each individual aircraft
The aircraft operator, for each individual aircraft
questions.explain: Approval is per aircraft and is applied for by the operator.

questions.question: An aeroplane extends its flaps on the approach. Which reading can change as a result of this alone?
options: The total air temperature reading
The static pressure reading
The angle of attack reading
questions.explain: The static source error depends on the position of the flaps, and it is the static pressure reading that this error affects.

questions.question: An aircraft climbs. What happens inside its barometric altimeter?
options: Pressure decreases, the bellows contract and the pointer rises
Pressure decreases, the bellows expand and the pointer rises
Pressure increases, the bellows expand and the pointer falls
questions.explain: Falling pressure around the capsule lets the bellows expand, which drives the pointer up the scale.

questions.question: One of the factors on which the choice of altimeter depends is
options: The number of static ports fitted
The tolerance values required by law
The transition level at the destination
questions.explain: Legal tolerance values are one of the three listed selection factors.

questions.question: An altimeter is left calibrated to 1013 hPa while the real pressure at sea level below the aircraft is lower. What will the instrument indicate?
options: Too high an altitude
The correct altitude
Too low an altitude
questions.explain: With the reference set higher than the real sea level pressure, the instrument over-reads.

questions.question: A jet aeroplane climbs from low altitude to high altitude. Which limit governs its maximum speed at the higher altitude?
options: The never exceed speed VNE
The maximum allowed Mach number MMO
The maximum operating velocity VMO
questions.explain: Above a certain altitude the Mach limit MMO takes over from the dynamic pressure limit VMO.

questions.question: A fast jet aeroplane cannot use the simple OAT indicating system. What is the reason?
options: It needs a bleed air supply that jets cannot provide
It cannot be protected against ice
It is only accurate up to an airspeed of 250 kts
questions.explain: Its accuracy runs out at 250 kts, which is why it is limited to slow aircraft.

questions.question: The temperature supply to an analogue air data computer is lost. Which outputs can no longer be produced?
options: Calibrated airspeed and altitude
Vertical speed and total air temperature
True airspeed and static air temperature
questions.explain: TAS and SAT are the outputs that depend on the temperature being supplied to the Mach module.

questions.question: A GNADIRU is fitted but the aircraft has no air data computer as a separate box. How does the unit obtain its pressures?
options: From air data modules placed as near as possible to the pitot and static sensors
From pneumatic tubes run from the probes to the unit in the avionics bay
From the inertial reference section, which derives the air data from accelerations
questions.explain: The air data section works like a digital air data computer but is fed digitally by modules mounted close to the probes and ports.

questions.question: After a deviation warning the aircraft goes on drifting away from the original altitude. At what point does the alert end?
options: When the aircraft is more than 900 ft from the original altitude
When the aircraft is more than 300 ft from the original altitude
When the aircraft reaches the altitude selected on the control panel
questions.explain: The deviation alert ends either on regaining the altitude or on passing 900 ft away from it.

questions.question: With which unit does the solid state flight recorder have a direct interface
options: the centralised data acquisition module
the flight warning computer
the flight management computer
questions.explain: Its direct interface is with the CDAM.

questions.question: When is the recorded data of the wireless quick access recorder compressed, encrypted and transmitted
options: while the aircraft is in the cruise
while the aircraft is being powered down
while the aircraft is on the ground
questions.explain: The transfer takes place with the aircraft on the ground.

questions.question: An exterior force has been applied to the axis of a running gyro and is held there. When does the gyro stop precessing?
options: when its axis has turned through a right angle from the direction it started in
when its sense of rotation corresponds to the rotational direction acting upon it
when the inertia of its rotating mass has fully absorbed the applied force
questions.explain: The gyro precesses until its sense of rotation corresponds to the rotational direction acting upon it.

questions.question: A unit on the bench is labelled as a directional gyro. What does that tell a technician about the way its spin axis lies?
options: it is vertical
it is horizontal
it is at 45 degrees
questions.explain: Gyros with a horizontal axis are the ones called directional gyros.

questions.question: In a direct reading compass the damping medium changes volume with temperature. What compensates for this?
options: Bellows
Slots
Washers
questions.explain: Bellows take up the expansion and contraction of the damping fluid.

questions.question: A remote compass system is fitted to an aircraft. Which two sensing devices does it use?
options: a sensor for the earth's magnetic field and a vertical gyro
a sensor for the aircraft's own field and a rate gyro
a sensor for the earth's magnetic field and a directional gyro
questions.explain: The system pairs an earth's field sensor with a directional gyro.

questions.question: How does the master warning light behave for a level 3 warning
options: It flashes
It stays steady
It stays dark
questions.explain: The master warning light flashes for a level 3 warning.

questions.question: An aircraft penetrates the mode 4A boundary at 250 knots with the landing gear still retracted. Which message is generated?
options: TOO LOW TERRAIN
TOO LOW GEAR
TOO LOW FLAPS
questions.explain: With the gear still up the boundary is penetrated at 190 knots or below as TOO LOW GEAR, while the boundary that rises with airspeed to 1000 feet at 250 knots gives TOO LOW TERRAIN.

questions.question: An operator does not want the TWENTY FIVE HUNDRED callout at 2500 feet. Which callout can be selected instead?
options: The MINIMUMS MINIMUMS callout
The RADIO ALTITUDE callout
The TOO LOW TERRAIN callout
questions.explain: At 2500 feet the alternative to TWENTY FIVE HUNDRED is the aural RADIO ALTITUDE.

questions.question: The input of a D-regulator changes at a constant rate. What does the output value do?
options: It increases linearly without limit
It falls back towards zero
It remains steady at one level
questions.explain: The differential regulator reacts to rate of change, so a steady rate gives a steady output.

questions.question: A quantity describing a linear motion of the aircraft is to be regulated. Which part of the autopilot has this task?
options: The outer loops, since the quantity is a flight condition parameter
The inner loop, since the quantity is a flight path parameter
The outer loops, since the quantity is a flight path parameter
questions.explain: Linear motion means a flight path parameter, and flight path regulation is the outer loop task.

questions.question: The roll channel of the autopilot/flight director is working as an independent subsystem. Why can it not guide the aircraft along a horizontal profile?
options: It needs the pitch channel to be engaged in a vertical profile mode
It needs inputs from the pilot or from a flight management computer system
It needs the auto-thrust system to set a flight phase thrust rating
questions.explain: On its own the roll channel has nothing to steer to, so it must be fed by the pilot or the FMCS.

questions.question: The crew must leave the FMS profile at short notice after an air traffic control request, but wishes to keep the autopilot flying. Which level of guidance do they use?
options: Selected manual
Selected automatic
Managed automatic
questions.explain: Selected automatic leaves the autopilot in control while the pilot supplies the reference values himself.

questions.question: The pilot pushes firmly on the control column while the autopilot is engaged. What happens to the auto-trim function?
options: It is transferred to the elevator actuator
It is deactivated until the force is removed
It is switched over to its high trim speed
questions.explain: Force on the control column deactivates auto-trim for as long as it is applied.

questions.question: The flight management system requests a climb. Why must the autoflight system have a pilot input before it starts that climb?
options: To prevent the autothrust system reverting to thrust mode
To prevent the flight management system losing its reference
To prevent altitude changes being made without ATC clearance
questions.explain: The pilot input stands in for the clearance, so the aircraft never changes level on its own.

questions.question: An aircraft tracking a radial passes overhead the VOR station. Why does the VOR mode need a separate over station phase?
options: Because the deviation signal is useless in the cone of confusion
Because the receiver frequency must be re-tuned as the station is passed
Because the pre-selected course must be reversed as the station is passed
questions.explain: With no usable deviation overhead, the controller cannot keep steering on it and needs another rule.

questions.question: Why is the yaw alignment left until shortly before touchdown
options: It minimizes the lateral drift
It minimizes the crosswind component
It minimizes the rudder deflection
questions.explain: Once the crab is taken out the aircraft starts drifting sideways, so the manoeuvre is kept short.

questions.question: The reported runway visual range is 100 m and the decision height is 40 ft — which category covers it?
options: CAT III a
CAT III b
CAT III c
questions.explain: A decision height below 50 ft with a visual range between 200 m and 75 m falls in CAT III b.

questions.question: An approach is flown to a decision height of 250 ft with a reported visual range of 600 m — which category applies?
options: CAT I
CAT II
CAT III a
questions.explain: A decision height of not less than 200 ft together with a visual range of not less than 550 m is CAT I.

questions.question: An airport has no runway visual range measuring equipment — which value may be converted instead?
options: The meteorological visibility
The cloud base height measured
The decision height selected
questions.explain: Met visibility can be converted where no RVR equipment exists.

questions.question: A low visibility take-off is a take-off made below a runway visual range of
options: 400 metres
550 metres
300 metres
questions.explain: Below 400 m RVR the departure counts as a low visibility take-off.

questions.question: One of several parallel channels drops out and the output signal is unaffected — which redundancy is in use?
options: Monitored redundancy
Passive redundancy
Active redundancy
questions.explain: Only active redundancy keeps the output going with no switch over.

questions.question: What is the leading edge of a rotor blade
options: The edge opposite the one that cuts into the wind
The outer end of the blade opposite the root
The edge that cuts into the wind as the blade turns
questions.explain: The leading edge cuts into the wind.

questions.question: Pitch angle and angle of attack are measured from different references. Which pairing of references is correct?
options: Pitch angle is referenced to the axis of rotation, angle of attack to the span line
Pitch angle is referenced to the plane of rotation, angle of attack to the relative wind
Pitch angle is referenced to the relative wind, angle of attack to the plane of rotation
questions.explain: Both use the chord, but pitch angle uses the plane of rotation and angle of attack uses the relative wind.

questions.question: On a turning blade the relative wind does not lie in the direction of the plane of rotation. What follows for the pitch angle and the angle of attack?
options: They cannot be equal to each other
They must change at the same rate
They must be equal to each other
questions.explain: The two angles are equal only when the relative wind has the same direction as the plane of rotation, so with the relative wind elsewhere they cannot be equal.

questions.question: A pilot pushes the cyclic stick forward to fly forward. Which chain of events takes place at the swash plate and the blades?
options: The swash plate is lifted, the control rods move and the blade pitch rises on every blade at once
The swash plate turns, the bell cranks move and the blade pitch is held through the revolution
The swash plate tilts, the control rods move and the blade pitch varies through the revolution
questions.explain: A cyclic input tilts the swash plate, which moves the control rods and varies blade pitch through each revolution.

questions.question: A helicopter flies forward at a steady speed. Why can its blades not all produce the same lift?
options: The airstream raises the pitch angle on one half of the disc and lowers it on the other
The airstream increases the rotational speed of the whole rotor disc
The airstream adds to the speed of one half of the disc and subtracts from the other
questions.explain: The airstream caused by the speed of flight is added to the rotational speed of the advancing blade and subtracted from that of the retreating blade, so the two sides of the disc cannot make the same lift.

questions.question: A reading light and a night illumination light both fail in the same cabin section. Why are two different subsystems involved?
options: Reading lights belong to the services system and night illumination to the address system
Reading lights belong to the lighting system and night illumination to the services system
Reading lights belong to the services system and night illumination to the lighting system
questions.explain: Reading lights sit under the Passenger Services System while night illumination sits under the Cabin Lighting System.

questions.question: Further functions are to be added to an existing NICE installation. Which protocol makes the system easy to expand?
options: The standard TCP/IP protocol
The ARINC 429 protocol
The spanning tree protocol
questions.explain: Expandability comes from the use of the standard TCP/IP protocol.

questions.question: An instrument is to be fitted in the middle at the top of a Basic T panel and must also display the indication from the flight director system. Which indicator is required?
options: The HSI
The ADI
The turn coordinator
questions.explain: The middle top position of the Basic T carries the attitude indicator, and the ADI is the attitude indicator that also shows the flight director indication.

questions.question: An aircraft can no longer hold its selected flight level unless the pilot flies manually. Which requirement for flight in RVSM airspace is no longer met?
options: An autopilot that can maintain the altitude
A device for indicating when leaving the predetermined height
A transponder with altitude transmission
questions.explain: One of the listed items of RVSM equipment is an autopilot able to maintain the altitude, and that is the function lost.

questions.question: In a Bourdon tube gauge the movement of the tube tip is proportional to
options: The applied pressure
The tube temperature
The signal frequency
questions.explain: Tip travel is proportional to the applied pressure.

questions.question: Two lines are parted at a quick-disconnect during maintenance. What happens at the coupling?
options: It stays open until a cap is fitted
It vents the line to ambient air
It seals itself automatically
questions.explain: A self-sealing coupling closes the line itself the moment it is parted.

questions.question: The same static line leak is considered in an unpressurized aircraft and in a pressurized one. How does the altimeter behave in each case?
options: It decreases the indication in the unpressurized aircraft and slightly increases it in the pressurized one
It slightly increases the indication in the unpressurized aircraft and decreases it in the pressurized one
It slightly increases the indication in both aircraft
questions.explain: With an unpressurized cabin the leak lowers the pressure in the static lines, so the altimeter reads slightly higher, while cabin pressure entering the lines of a pressurized aircraft raises that pressure, so it reads lower.

questions.question: The pitot tube becomes totally blocked in cruise and the thrust is then increased to accelerate. What does the airspeed indicator show?
options: No change in the indicated speed
A rise in the indicated speed
A fall in the indicated speed to zero
questions.explain: At constant altitude neither pressure changes, so the reading is frozen whatever the thrust.

questions.question: The temperature indication is needed in order to determine
options: IAS
EAS
TAS
questions.explain: The temperature display is used among other things for determining the TAS.

questions.question: In flight, how do the three measured air temperature values compare with one another?
options: SAT is the highest, RAT is lower than SAT but higher than TAT
TAT is the highest, RAT is lower than TAT but higher than SAT
RAT is the highest, TAT is lower than RAT but higher than SAT
questions.explain: Full ram rise gives the highest value at the TAT probe, RAT loses part of it, and SAT has none.

questions.question: A hybrid air data computer is described as hybrid because
options: it uses both pressure capsules and pressure transducers
it can be supplied with either AC or DC power
it provides outputs in analogue as well as digital form
questions.explain: The mixture of analogue and digital outputs is what makes the computer hybrid.

questions.question: An air data module at a pitot probe has converted the pressure it senses. Which path does the resulting signal then follow?
options: To an air data inertial reference unit, and from there on to the user systems
To the display management computers, and from there on to an air data inertial reference unit
To the standby instruments, and from there on to an air data inertial reference unit
questions.explain: The module feeds the ADIRU, which is the computer that produces the air data outputs for the displays and other systems.

questions.question: An angle of attack sensor is a tube lying crosswise to the air stream, pierced by two rows of holes. How does it sense the angle?
options: by measuring the total pressure at the forward row
by sensing the movement of the stagnation point between the rows
by comparing the pressures sensed at the two rows
questions.explain: The tube senses the angle as a pressure difference between its two rows of holes.

questions.question: Besides recording and storing digital flight data, the wireless quick access recorder is also able to
options: transmit the digital flight data to the ground
format the digital flight data for the recorder
erase the digital flight data after transfer
questions.explain: Recording, storing and wireless transmission are the three stated purposes.

questions.question: A main gearbox has no cockpit instrument or warning of its own. Why does that make its speed probe reading so valuable?
options: Because a vibration there could otherwise be felt through the controls
Because an overheat there could otherwise be read on the oil gauge
Because an overspeed there could otherwise go unidentified by the crew
questions.explain: Components the crew cannot watch are exactly the ones whose overspeed the probe would otherwise miss.

questions.question: A commercial aircraft is fitted with electrical directional gyros. How is their drift dealt with?
options: It is compensated by the pilot each hour
It is compensated automatically
It is compensated by the vertical gyro
questions.explain: Electrical gyros in commercial aircraft carry automatic drift compensation.

questions.question: Some error is still left after a compass has been compensated — where is that remainder written down?
options: on a label fitted beside the flux valve
on the compensating disc at the airport site
on a deviation card carried on the aircraft
questions.explain: The remaining deviation goes on the deviation card that stays on the aircraft.

questions.question: A pushbutton is lit in a colour that reports normal operation. Which two colours can be used for that?
options: Red or amber
Amber or white
Green or blue
questions.explain: Green and blue are the two colours for normal operation, green for a backup system and blue for a temporarily used system.

questions.question: How many chimes are sounded for a level 2 caution
options: None
Three
One
questions.explain: A level 2 caution is given with a single chime.

questions.question: A recorder fault and a stall warning occur on the same flight. How do the two alerts differ in what the crew receives?
options: One gives a single chime while the other gives no sound
Each one gives an aural alarm but only one gives a light
One gives no sound or light while the other gives both
questions.explain: A recorder fault is a level 1 with no aural alarm or warning light, while a stall warning is a level 3 with an aural alarm and a flashing master warning light.

questions.question: The limits of one of the alerting envelopes are exceeded. What does the enhanced ground proximity warning system give the flight crew?
options: Aural alert messages with visual annunciations and displays
An automatic pull-up commanded through the autopilot
A master warning that has to be reset by the crew
questions.explain: Exceeding an envelope limit produces aural messages together with visual annunciations and displays.

questions.question: A pilot reads the rotor rpm on the triple tachometer. Which part of the dial shows it?
options: The large pointer N1 on the outer scale
The digital window at the foot of the dial
The small pointer R on the inner scale
questions.explain: Rotor rpm is the small R pointer on the inner scale.

questions.question: Which motions are described by flight condition parameters
options: oscillatory motions
rotary motions
translatory motions
questions.explain: Flight condition parameters belong to the rotary degrees of freedom.

questions.question: Vertical speed is treated as a basic mode by some autopilots. Why is this called an exception?
options: Vertical speed is in fact a flight path parameter
Vertical speed is in fact named after a flight phase
Vertical speed is in fact a flight condition parameter
questions.explain: Basic modes normally hold flight condition parameters, and vertical speed is not one.

questions.question: Whether an overpowering of the flight controls leads to disengagement depends on
options: The mode selected and the channel that is engaged
The circumstances of the input and the autopilot itself
The torque the limiter is built to pass and the airspeed
questions.explain: Disengagement is made conditional on both the pilot's input and the design of the autopilot.

questions.question: During the synchronization phase the pitch regulator produces no actuator activity at all. Why is that so?
options: The regulator output is clamped, so the actuator cannot respond
The momentary pitch angle is compared with itself, so the error is zero
The momentary pitch angle is held at zero, so the error is zero
questions.explain: Both inputs to the summing point are the same signal, so the error is always zero.

questions.question: The autopilot banks the aircraft into a turn and must not let it descend. Why does the elevator have to be deflected as well?
options: Total lift must rise so its vertical part still balances the weight
Total lift must fall so its horizontal part still curves the path
Total drag must rise so the airspeed stays at the reference value
questions.explain: Banking tilts the lift, so total lift must be increased to keep the vertical part equal to the weight.

questions.question: The localizer mode has been selected on its own on the autoflight control panel as an independent lateral mode — which phase is left out?
options: The Capture Phase
The Approach-Track Phase
The Localizer-Track Phase
questions.explain: Selecting LOC as an independent lateral mode omits the Approach-Track Phase.

questions.question: An aircraft is at 300 ft AGL with the Approach/Land mode engaged and the crew presses the Approach button again — what happens?
options: The mode reverts to the localizer submode
The mode disengages immediately
The mode stays in operation
questions.explain: Below 400 ft the button press no longer deactivates the mode.

questions.question: The decrab is being flown on an automatic landing — which reference is the heading aligned with?
options: The present track
The localizer deviation
The preselected course
questions.explain: The align phase flies the heading onto the preselected course.

questions.question: The yaw bar in the ADI deflects during the take off run. Which control inputs does the pilot make?
options: Aileron or roll spoiler inputs
Rudder or nose wheel steering inputs
Elevator or stabiliser trim inputs
questions.explain: Yaw bar commands are flown with rudder or nose wheel steering.

questions.question: The aircraft climbs through a radio altitude of 30 ft after lift off. What changes in the flight director?
options: The roll channel is deactivated and the yaw channel activated
The yaw channel is deactivated and the roll channel activated
The pitch channel is deactivated and the roll channel activated
questions.explain: At 30 ft the yaw channel drops out and the roll channel comes in at the same moment.

questions.question: An approach is planned to a decision height of 150 ft with a reported visual range of 400 m — which category applies?
options: CAT II
CAT III a
CAT I
questions.explain: A decision height between 200 ft and 100 ft with at least 300 m visual range is CAT II.

questions.question: A single autopilot is engaged and it detects its own failure and disengages. Which behaviour does the system show?
options: fail operational behaviour
fail passive behaviour
fail safe behaviour
questions.explain: A single system able to detect and remove its own failure gives fail passive behaviour in single operation.

questions.question: A single failure occurs below the alert height and degrades the failure mode from fail operational to fail passive. What happens to the displayed capability?
options: it is no longer changed
it drops by one category
it is replaced by a red warning
questions.explain: Below the alert height the capability is frozen even though the failure mode degrades.

questions.question: Two reference dimensions of a rotor blade are quoted, one measured along the blade centreline and one across the blade section. Which pair is correct?
options: Span along the centreline, chord across the section
Span along the centreline, root across the section
Chord along the centreline, span across the section
questions.explain: Span runs root to tip along the centreline, and the chord runs leading edge to trailing edge across the section.

questions.question: A helicopter rotor turns counterclockwise. The tip-path plane must tilt backward for rearward flight. Following the precession rule, where must the downward force be applied?
options: On the left side
Right at the rear
On the right side
questions.explain: The output is wanted at the rear; 90° earlier in counterclockwise rotation is the left side.

questions.question: Gyroscopic precession is
options: The change of the rotational axis as a result of an external force
The change of the rotor RPM as a result of an external force
The turning of the fuselage opposite to the rotor
questions.explain: Precession is a change of the rotational axis caused by an external force.

questions.question: An engine fails and the helicopter enters autorotation. What control does the pilot have?
options: No control, and the helicopter lands where the descent takes it
Full control, including the choice of the touchdown point
Pedal control only, with no choice of touchdown point
questions.explain: During an autorotative landing the helicopter stays fully controllable and the pilot determines the location for touchdown.

questions.question: During hover, tail rotor thrust makes the helicopter drift to the right. How must the main rotor disk be tilted to prevent this?
options: Slightly forward
Slightly to the right
Slightly to the left
questions.explain: The disk is tilted opposite to the drift, so to the left for a right drift.

questions.question: The same power source that feeds the public address system also feeds other loads that stay powered when every other source is inoperative. How must those other loads be treated?
options: Those other loads are taken into account in the powering duration
Those other loads are transferred to the crew interphone supply
Those other loads are shed for the whole powering duration
questions.explain: The duration must be achieved while considering the other loads left on the same source.

questions.question: Video, announcements and recorded audio all have to reach a seat. Which subsystem controls and distributes them to it?
options: The Passenger Services System
The Passenger Entertainment System
The Cabin Interphone System
questions.explain: All three are routed to the seat through the Passenger Entertainment System.

questions.question: Why are static ports placed in areas where turbulence and ram air distortion are low
options: Because turbulence and ram air distortion overheat the static port zones
Because turbulence and ram air distortion block the static pressure hoses
Because turbulence and ram air distortion falsify the static pressure reading
questions.explain: A port in a quiet zone senses the true static pressure, while turbulence and ram air distortion at the port falsify that reading.

questions.question: A Prandtl tube delivers Ptot and Ps to a computer. Which quantity does the computer obtain from them, and what is it needed for?
options: The ram pressure, needed for the speed indication
The total air temperature, needed for the speed indication
The static source error, needed for the altitude indication
questions.explain: The differential of the two delivered pressures is the ram pressure q, which is what the speed indication requires.

questions.question: The limits for damage to the skin at the static ports are found
options: In the ATA chapter for the instruments or the IPC
In the ATA chapter for the aircraft structure or the SRM
In the ATA chapter for air conditioning or the wiring manual
questions.explain: Skin damage is a structural item, so the structure chapter or the SRM holds those limits.

questions.question: Why can water be present in the pressure pipes
options: They are not drained on a regular basis
They are capped for protection during testing
Their test fittings are used to simulate altitude and speed
questions.explain: The pipes are not drained routinely, so water can collect in them.

questions.question: TAS is obtained from IAS by correcting for instrument error, static source error, dynamic pressure error and
options: Magnetic variation
Aircraft weight
Air density
questions.explain: Air density is the fourth correction listed for deriving TAS from IAS.

questions.question: An aircraft with an IVSI enters and leaves a turn with a high bank angle. What should be expected?
options: A correct vertical speed indication, because the piston compensates for bank angle
An inaccurate vertical speed indication, because any vertical acceleration affects the piston
A total loss of indication, because the piston is locked by the acceleration
questions.explain: Any vertical acceleration acts on the piston, so turn entry and exit give a wrong reading.

questions.question: A servo corrected altimeter reads a long way from the altitude sent by the air data computer. Why does the correction not bring it into agreement?
options: Correction is inhibited while the internal vibrator is running
Correction only works above the altitude set on the baro scale
Correction is only possible within a few hundred feet
questions.explain: Continuous correction requires the error voltage to be about zero, which limits it to a few hundred feet.

questions.question: An air data computer stops working altogether. What is seen on the Mach/airspeed indicator?
options: A red flag for the Mach value only, because CAS is taken from a capsule
A red flag for each value, because the valid discretes are no longer transmitted
No flag at all, because the indicator holds the last values received
questions.explain: Loss of the valid discrete for a value raises the red flag for that value.

questions.question: An aeroplane gives no noticeable initial buffet as its speed decays towards the point of lift loss. What must be installed?
options: A stall warning system
An altitude alert system
An angle of attack indicator
questions.explain: A stall warning system must be installed when the approaching stall speed is not immediately noticeable through initial buffet.

questions.question: The altitude readout box on the PFD changes from white to yellow. Which mode has the system entered?
options: Deviation mode
Capture mode
Approach mode
questions.explain: A white to yellow change of the altitude readout box marks the deviation mode.

questions.question: Health and usage monitoring systems are a common part of the flight avionics of
options: a modern large aeroplane
a modern helicopter
a modern business jet
questions.explain: Health and usage monitoring systems are a common component in the flight avionics of modern helicopters.

questions.question: A free gyroscope is left standing at the equator. Which of the two apparent errors is at its greatest there?
options: transport wander
apparent drift
apparent topple
questions.explain: Apparent topple is greatest at the equator.

questions.question: On which law of magnetism is the function of the magnetic compass based
options: Unlike poles attract and like poles repel
All poles attract when they are close enough
Like poles attract and unlike poles repel
questions.explain: The main law of magnetism quoted is that unlike poles attract and like poles repel.

questions.question: Which colour indicates the normal operation of a temporarily used system
options: Blue
Green
Amber
questions.explain: Blue indicates the normal operation of a temporarily used system.

questions.question: The aural message SINK RATE has sounded but PULL UP has not. Which boundary has the aircraft penetrated?
options: The outer alert boundary
The upper alert boundary
The inner alert boundary
questions.explain: SINK RATE is the outer boundary message; PULL UP would mean the inner boundary had been crossed as well.

questions.question: The flaps are at the landing position and the aircraft is within two dots of the localizer on an ILS approach, so which submode boundary applies?
options: Mode 2A
Mode 4B
Mode 2B
questions.explain: That configuration is one of those listed for mode 2B.

questions.question: The aircraft drifts 1.5 dots below the beam centre at 800 feet radio altitude. Which alert, if any, is triggered?
options: The hard alert
No alert at all
The soft alert
questions.explain: The aircraft is beyond 1.3 dots below the beam centre, so the soft alert comes; the hard alert needs below 300 feet radio altitude and more than 2 dots.

questions.question: An aural message is heard and exactly seven seconds later the same words are heard again. Which envelope is still penetrated?
options: The warning envelope
The caution envelope
The clearance floor envelope
questions.explain: A seven second repeat is the caution level; the warning level repeats continuously.

questions.question: The fuel level in a tank changes. What does the multi-tubular surface condenser in the tank do?
options: It changes its capacity
It changes its excitation frequency
It changes its resistance
questions.explain: The condenser changes its capacity depending on the level of fuel in the tank.

questions.question: The output frequency of a densitometer is read. What is that frequency proportional to?
options: The fuel height
The fuel temperature
The fuel density
questions.explain: The frequency of the vibrations is proportional to the fuel density.

questions.question: A controlled system is acted on by disturbances whose effect cannot be predicted. Why is open loop control the wrong choice here?
options: It can only correct for what was allowed for in advance
It needs a measurement unit that unpredictable disturbances overload
It feeds the disturbance back and so amplifies the error further
questions.explain: Without feedback the correction must be worked out beforehand, which an unpredictable disturbance makes impossible.

questions.question: In a P-regulator the change in the output value is always proportional to
options: the magnitude of the input value
the change in the input value
the rate of change of the input value
questions.explain: A proportional regulator ties the change of its output directly to the change of its input.

questions.question: As the aircraft accelerates past a certain airspeed the maximum rudder deflection available is reduced. What does this limiting achieve?
options: It keeps the yaw damper inside its authority
It keeps the loads within the limits of structural strength
It keeps the surface within its maximum deflection angle
questions.explain: Because effectiveness grows with dynamic pressure, deflection is limited at speed to hold loads within structural limits.

questions.question: The autopilot is engaged while the aircraft is banked three degrees. What does the autopilot do?
options: It holds the three degrees of bank and lets the heading run
It rolls back to wings level and holds the heading of that moment
It rolls back to wings level and holds the last selected heading
questions.explain: Under five degrees the bank angle criterion selects heading hold on the heading present at engagement.

questions.question: An aircraft climbs through the changeover altitude with a speed target that was dialled in by hand. What becomes of the number in the window?
options: It is converted to the equivalent Mach number and displayed there
It is converted to the equivalent true airspeed and displayed there
It is replaced by dashes until the pilot enters a Mach number
questions.explain: At the transition the value is converted to the equivalent Mach number, and a value entered at the panel is shown there.

questions.question: In the vertical navigation modes, which channel performs the vertical guidance?
options: The pitch channel
The autothrust channel
The roll channel
questions.explain: Vertical guidance is a pitch task and thrust control is left to the autothrust.

questions.question: Beam convergence has been left uncompensated on an ILS approach — how does the glide path controller behave at long range and close in?
options: Sluggish far out and unable to hold the beam near the runway
Prone to oscillation far out and sluggish near the runway
Sluggish far out and prone to oscillation near the runway
questions.explain: Low gain far out makes it sluggish, and rising gain close in makes it oscillate.

questions.question: The preselected course is the reference for the align phase — what must the pilot check before the alignment?
options: That it agrees with the present heading
That it agrees with the runway heading
That it agrees with the localizer frequency
questions.explain: The align phase is only as good as the preselected course, so it must match the runway heading.

questions.question: A crosswind automatic landing is flown — what does the flight mode annunciator show as the yaw align phase begins?
options: ROLLOUT appears as the lateral mode
ALIGN appears as the lateral mode
Nothing at all is annunciated for it
questions.explain: The align phase gets no annunciation at all.

questions.question: Which channel and which surface does the align phase require
options: A roll channel acting on the ailerons
A yaw channel acting on the nose wheel
A yaw channel acting on the rudder
questions.explain: The decrab is flown by the yaw channel through the rudder.

questions.question: A large thrust increase at the start of a go around produces a strong nose up moment — which limits must the go around controller watch?
options: The pitch attitude or angle of attack limits
The bank angle or sideslip limits
The flap or landing gear speed limits
questions.explain: The required thrust increase causes a large positive pitch moment, so the pitch attitude and angle of attack limits have to be observed.

questions.question: An engine fails while the aircraft is accelerating and is still below V1. What must be done?
options: The take off has to be discontinued
The aircraft has to be rotated at once
The take off has to be continued
questions.explain: Before V1 an engine failure obliges the crew to stop the take off.

questions.question: The pitch channel is given the task of holding a certain altitude. Which system then controls the airspeed?
options: The pitch channel, which keeps its priority
The auto-throttle or auto-thrust system
The flight management system computer
questions.explain: The pitch channel delegates speed control once it is busy with another task.

questions.question: Which cockpit input changes the pitch angle of all main rotor blades
options: The tail rotor pedals
The cyclic pitch stick
The collective pitch control
questions.explain: The collective pitch control changes the pitch angle.

questions.question: A pilot raises the collective lever to climb and the torque effect on the fuselage changes. Which control must the pilot then use to vary the thrust that compensates it?
options: The tail rotor pedals
The collective lever
The cyclic pitch stick
questions.explain: Torque is compensated by the tail rotor, whose thrust the pilot varies with the pedals.

questions.question: A helicopter is hovering with no wind at all. Why is there no dissymmetry of lift in this condition?
options: There is no pitch angle on either blade, so both blades have the same parameters
There is no airstream due to forward speed, so both blades have the same parameters
There is no rotational speed at the blade tips, so both blades have the same parameters
questions.explain: Without the airstream caused by the speed of flight there is nothing to add to one blade and subtract from the other.

questions.question: Why does upward flapping reduce the angle of attack of the advancing blade?
options: Moving up reduces the blade pitch angle
Moving up adds a downward relative wind component
Moving up adds an upward relative wind component
questions.explain: Relative wind is opposite to blade motion, so an upward-moving blade meets air from above, reducing the angle of attack.

questions.question: Once the engine has failed, what does the collective pitch lever control
options: The tail rotor thrust that keeps the heading in the descent
The engine power that keeps the rotor turning in the descent
The force that keeps the rotor turning in the descent
questions.explain: With no engine the collective no longer sets engine power; it controls the force that sustains rotor RPM.

questions.question: Two operators want the cabin of the same aeroplane arranged to suit their own service. What does the CIDS design philosophy give them?
options: A fixed configuration set once by the airframe manufacturer
Flexibility gained by exchanging the cabin wiring looms
Flexibility without complex and time-consuming hardware changes
questions.explain: The CIDS is designed for high flexibility so that complex and time expensive hardware changes are not needed.

questions.question: For which aircraft is the NICE cabin management system offered
options: Long range freighter aircraft
VIP and government aircraft
Regional commuter aircraft
questions.explain: The system is offered for VIP and government aircraft.

questions.question: An exhaust gas temperature indicator is fitted in a classical cockpit. Which group and subdivision does it belong to?
options: Aircraft monitoring, as an engine monitoring device
Flight monitoring, as a pressure monitoring device
Aircraft monitoring, as an airframe monitoring device
questions.explain: Exhaust gas temperature indicators are named as engine monitoring devices under aircraft monitoring.

questions.question: One screen in the cockpit carries all the air data information and also every Basic T parameter. This screen is
options: the HSI (Horizontal Situation Indicator)
the PFD (Primary Flight Display)
the standby horizon
questions.explain: The PFD is the screen that holds all the air data information, and it shows every one of the Basic T parameters.

questions.question: The pitot probe of a simple system becomes completely blocked while the static system stays clear. Which of the instruments supplied by that system is affected?
options: The airspeed indicator
The altimeter
The vertical speed indicator
questions.explain: Of the three instruments only the airspeed indicator uses pitot pressure, so only it depends on the pitot probe.

questions.question: The Mach module of an analogue air data computer fails. Why is the static source error correction affected as well?
options: The correction depends primarily on the calibrated airspeed, which comes from that module
The correction depends on the static pressure, which is routed through the Mach module
The correction depends primarily on the Mach number, which comes from that module
questions.explain: Static source error depends first of all on Mach number, and that value is supplied by the Mach module.

questions.question: The static pressure reaching an analogue air data computer is in error. What is the effect of this on the Mach indication
options: The Mach number stays correct, because the Mach module has a pressure input of its own
The Mach number is wrong as well, because the Mach module works from the other two modules
The Mach number is wrong as well, because the Mach module works from the temperature input
questions.explain: The Mach module takes its information from the altitude and airspeed modules, both of which use the static pressure, so an error in that pressure carries into the Mach number.

questions.question: An aircraft climbs steadily and the MMO limit falls. Why does it fall?
options: Because the dynamic pressure decreases
Because the compressibility error increases
Because the speed of sound decreases
questions.explain: The falling speed of sound is the stated reason.

questions.question: An aircraft makes only small changes of height. What happens to the coarse synchro value in the electrical altimeter?
options: It is blocked by the OFF flag monitor
It is blocked by the LIMITER
It is blocked by the HIGH LEVEL detector
questions.explain: For small height changes the fine value alone is used and the HIGH LEVEL detector blocks the coarse value.

questions.question: How does the air data computer obtain true airspeed from equivalent airspeed?
options: It adds the static source error correction to the equivalent airspeed
It replaces the standard pressure used before with the real pressure
It replaces the standard density used before with the real density
questions.explain: The step from EAS to TAS is the substitution of real air density for standard density.

questions.question: The analogue output data of a hybrid air data computer is provided in the format
options: ARINC 629
ARINC 429
ARINC 565
questions.explain: ARINC 565 is the analogue format, ARINC 429 the digital one.

questions.question: A digital air data computer has lost its angle of attack, flap and gear position inputs. Which of its functions is degraded?
options: The corrections, such as the static source error correction
The conversion of the input pressures into electrical signals
The transmission of the computed values on the output busses
questions.explain: Those inputs are used for the data corrections, so only the correction accuracy suffers.

questions.question: Air data modules are located near the static port or pitot probe, where they
options: amplify the air pressure for transmission along the tubes
convert the air pressure directly into a digital word
convert the air pressure into a proportional analogue voltage
questions.explain: Conversion to a digital data word happens at the module, right by the sensing point.

questions.question: Engineering wants an engine left on the wing as long as it is sound, yet changed at the home base before it causes trouble. Which installed system makes that possible?
options: The on board maintenance system, which stores reported faults
The flight data recording system, which records for the investigators
The monitoring system, which records data from various systems
questions.explain: Only the monitoring system records condition data that lets a part be used to its limit and still be changed at base.

questions.question: An operator wants more than 25 hours of flight parameters held in the recorder. What makes that possible?
options: Using a shorter word than twelve bits
Using a second recorder in parallel with the first
Using the right combination of capacity and data rate
questions.explain: Storage beyond 25 hours comes from matching recorder capacity with data rate.

questions.question: An aircraft is fitted with a glass cockpit. How is the rate of turn presented to its crew?
options: by the ball of the inclinometer
on an electronic display
on a pointer over a mechanical scale
questions.explain: In a glass cockpit the rate of turn appears on a display.

questions.question: A compass measures heading with a mounted, freely rotating permanent magnet. Which method is this and which kind of compass?
options: The mechanical method, a direct reading compass
The mechanical method, a remote reading compass
The electronic method, a remote reading compass
questions.explain: The magnetic needle principle is the mechanical method and gives the direct reading compass.

questions.question: An aircraft is fitted with only the minimum number of display computers, so what does it lack compared with a large aircraft?
options: The computer that drives the centre displays
The computer that is there for redundancy
The computer that handles the analogue inputs
questions.explain: The minimum fit is two computers, so the third one carried for redundancy on large aircraft is missing.

questions.question: A pilot selects the ILS mode on his ND, so which two deviations does he then see?
options: Localizer and glideslope
Localizer and track
Glideslope and vertical speed
questions.explain: The ILS mode of the ND indicates localizer and glideslope deviation.

questions.question: The take-off configuration check is run with a cabin door still open, so what will the crew find?
options: The normal message will not appear
The check will be bypassed automatically
The master caution will be inhibited
questions.explain: Door closed is one of the items checked, so an open door prevents the normal result.

questions.question: Until when do the mode 3 visual annunciators remain active
options: Until the landing gear has been retracted
Until the warning envelope has been left
Until a positive rate of climb is established
questions.explain: They stay active until a positive rate of climb exists.

questions.question: An engine vibration reading is seen in the cockpit, so how is its level expressed?
options: Usually in millimetres
Usually in units
Usually in percent
questions.explain: The cockpit indication is normally given in units.

questions.question: What do the regulations demand for the operating states or modes of the autoflight subsystems?
options: Feedback to the pilot by an aural warning tone
Feedback to the pilot by coloured annunciators
Feedback to the flight management system by a data bus
questions.explain: The rules call for the modes to be annunciated to the pilot in colour.

questions.question: Which connection is actually made when an autopilot is engaged
options: The torque limiter connecting the AP-servo with the trim actuator
The servo valve connecting the AP-servo with the hydraulic supply
The clutch connecting the AP-servo with the primary controls
questions.explain: Engagement is the closing of the clutch between the AP-servo and the primary flight controls.

questions.question: A pilot holds a steady force on the control wheel in CWS. What do the inner loops produce from it, and what does the aircraft do?
options: A proportional roll rate, which changes the attitude and the heading
A fixed roll rate, which changes the heading but not the attitude
A proportional roll angle, which changes the turn rate and the track
questions.explain: The force becomes a proportional roll rate, and a lasting roll rate changes the attitude and so the heading.

questions.question: An upper pitch mode is switched off in flight on an aircraft whose basic pitch mode holds the momentary rate of climb. Which mode does the autopilot then adopt?
options: Altitude hold mode
Altitude acquisition mode
Vertical speed mode
questions.explain: Where vertical speed is the basic mode, switching off any upper vertical mode leaves the autopilot in vertical speed.

questions.question: An aircraft is levelling off in altitude acquisition mode above the transition level. Which reference is the selected target expressed against?
options: A radio height above ground
A QNH corrected altitude
A pressure altitude
questions.explain: Above the transition level flight levels are flown on standard setting, so the target is a pressure altitude.

questions.question: The crew has not pressed the altitude hold button. Under what condition does the altitude hold mode still come in automatically?
options: On approaching a pre-selected altitude with acquisition armed
On approaching a pre-selected altitude with acquisition active
On passing the transition altitude during a climb or descent
questions.explain: The acquisition must already be running, not merely armed, for the hold to follow automatically.

questions.question: The aircraft is being steered along the centre line after landing — which two signals does the yaw controller process?
options: The heading error and the glide path deviation
The crab angle and the localizer deviation
The heading error and the localizer deviation
questions.explain: Both a heading error and a lateral displacement have to be removed, so both signals are used.

questions.question: An aircraft is flying on a path whose angle equals its potential flight path angle — what are its errors?
options: Airspeed error zero and flight path error zero
Airspeed error at a maximum and flight path error at a maximum
Airspeed error zero and flight path error not zero
questions.explain: Flying at the potential angle means the energy is exactly balanced, so both errors vanish.

questions.question: The aircraft accelerates in the cruise — what happens to the yaw rate signal passed on to the actuator?
options: It is cut back as the speed rises
It is built up as the speed rises
It is held at its take-off value
questions.explain: Inverse proportionality means the signal is reduced as speed increases.

questions.question: The fail passive automatic flight control system fails during an approach. What must happen then?
options: the system continues the approach and landing by itself
the pilot has to take over the control of the aircraft
the second autopilot takes over control and lands
questions.explain: On failure of a fail passive system the pilot has to take over control.

questions.question: The autopilot of a hybrid landing installation fails on short final. How can the landing still be completed?
options: manually, following the supporting guidance system
automatically, by the second autopilot taking over
automatically, after the voter has selected a channel
questions.explain: The hybrid system's reserve is manual flight on the supporting guidance system, not a second automatic system.

questions.question: The cyclic stick is moved to the left-hand side. Which servo stays unenergized and which movement results?
options: the front servo, and the helicopter moves nose down
the LH servo, and the helicopter moves sideways to the left
the front servo, and the helicopter moves sideways to the left
questions.explain: A sideward input leaves the front servo unenergized and moves the helicopter sideward to the left.

questions.question: The SCAS has received a rate signal from one of the gyros. What does it drive with its attenuation signal?
options: the trim actuators of the cyclic stick
the servo valves of the control servos
the main servo input levers directly
questions.explain: The attenuation signals go to the servo valves of the control servos.

questions.question: Which force produced by the main rotor blades holds the helicopter up against gravity?
options: Thrust
Lift
Drag
questions.explain: Of the two forces the airfoil produces, lift is the one the manual gives as counteracting gravity.

questions.question: A helicopter is in forward flight and one blade is on the advancing side. In which direction does the relative wind on that blade act?
options: Horizontally backward, opposite to the blade movement
Horizontally forward, with the blade movement
Backward and upward, across the blade movement
questions.explain: The advancing blade moves forward, and the relative wind is always opposite to the blade's flight path.

questions.question: What must happen to the plane of rotation when an external force tilts the axis of rotation
options: It tilts with the axis, staying perpendicular to it
It tilts the opposite way, staying parallel to the axis
It stays level, while the axis tilts away from it
questions.explain: The plane of rotation is always perpendicular to the axis of rotation, so it tilts with the axis.

questions.question: A rotor head is built with no flapping hinges at all. How can dissymmetry of lift still be balanced on this rotor?
options: The lead-lag hinges let the blades move up and down instead
The blades themselves flex and absorb the forces acting on them
The feathering hinges let the blades change pitch instead
questions.explain: Where there is no flapping hinge, the blades must instead have properties that allow them to absorb the forces.

questions.question: Which turning force does a counterclockwise turning main rotor generate on the fuselage
options: A nose-down pitching force
A clockwise turning force
A counterclockwise turning force
questions.explain: The fuselage force is opposite, so clockwise.

questions.question: A microphone has been left out of its stowage and unused at a cabin crew station. What must the public address system do in that condition?
options: Remain fully operative in the cabin
Become inoperative until that microphone is stowed
Mute the loudspeakers in that cabin zone
questions.explain: No unused, un-stowed microphone may render the system inoperative, so the system has to remain fully operative.

questions.question: Which three things does the Cabin Intercommunication Data System do to the cabin systems it serves
options: Controls, tests and monitors them
Controls, records and displays them
Tests, records and announces them
questions.explain: Control, test and monitor are the three functions printed for the CIDS.

questions.question: A pilot reads his magnetic heading and a VOR course deviation from one round instrument. Which indicator is he using?
options: The HSI
The ADI
The variometer
questions.explain: The HSI is the instrument that combines compass and radio navigation information.

questions.question: How does the temperature behave with increasing height in the troposphere
options: It decreases by 6.5 °C every 100 metres
It increases by 0.65 °C every 100 metres
It decreases by 0.65 °C every 100 metres
questions.explain: The troposphere lapse rate is 0.65 °C per 100 m of climb.

questions.question: The indications fluctuate during a check of the pitot static system. What does this show?
options: The presence of water in the pressure pipes
The presence of ice at the static port
The presence of a leak in the pressure pipes
questions.explain: Fluctuating indications are the sign of water lying in the pipes.

questions.question: A new reference pressure is selected on an electrical altitude indicator. How is the correction made?
options: Pneumatically, by an additional set of bellows
Mechanically, by turning the whole altimeter mechanism
Electrically, in the instrument or in an air data computer
questions.explain: Electrical indicators have no mechanism to turn, so the correction is done electrically.

questions.question: Why can the speed limit of a jet aeroplane at low altitude be read directly as an indicated airspeed?
options: Because the limit there depends on the speed of sound, and the airspeed indicator measures dynamic pressure
Because the limit there depends on dynamic pressure, and the airspeed indicator measures total pressure
Because the limit there depends on dynamic pressure, and the airspeed indicator measures dynamic pressure
questions.explain: The indicated airspeed is a dynamic pressure indicator, and at low altitudes the limit depends on the dynamic pressure acting on the aircraft structure, so that limit can be marked as a speed.

questions.question: A machmeter is opened and found to contain a differential pressure capsule and an aneroid capsule. Which instruments use these same two sensing elements?
options: The altimeter uses a differential pressure capsule and the airspeed indicator an aneroid capsule
The airspeed indicator uses a differential pressure capsule and the altimeter an aneroid capsule
The airspeed indicator uses a differential pressure capsule and the vertical speed indicator an aneroid capsule
questions.explain: The airspeed indicator measures with a differential pressure capsule and the altimeter with an aneroid capsule, and a mach meter contains both of those bellows.

questions.question: The data supplied by the air data components of a GNADIRU comprises
options: attitude, heading, vertical acceleration and body rates
airspeed, Mach, angle of attack, temperature and barometric altitude
present position, satellite status and receiver clock error
questions.explain: These are the air data outputs; attitude and position come from the other two sections.

questions.question: An altitude deviation occurs in the cruise. What does the crew get on EICAS and aurally?
options: The warning message ALTITUDE ALERT with Master Warning and a bell
An advisory message ALTITUDE ALERT with no aural indication
The caution message ALTITUDE ALERT with Master Caution and the owl tone
questions.explain: It is a caution level alert with Master Caution and an owl tone.

questions.question: What does a running gyroscope tend to do
options: align its axis with the earth's magnetic field
maintain the direction of its axis in space
hold its axis square to the aircraft structure
questions.explain: The gyroscope makes every effort to maintain the direction of its axis in space.

questions.question: What is the horizontal component of apparent wander called
options: apparent drift
transport wander
apparent topple
questions.explain: The horizontal component of apparent wander is apparent drift.

questions.question: A gyro has worn frame bearings and is also carried east-west across the earth. How do the two error sources add up?
options: the bearing error takes the place of the earth rotation and transport errors
the bearing error sits on top of the earth rotation and transport errors
the bearing error is cancelled by the earth rotation and transport errors
questions.explain: Real errors from construction are error values over and above those due to the earth's rotation and transport.

questions.question: A gyro on the bench has its rotational axis standing upright. Which measuring task is it built for?
options: turn rate measurement
attitude measurement
directional measurement
questions.explain: The vertical axis gyro is the attitude gyro, so it does attitude measurement.

questions.question: The gyro axis points at the centre of the earth during unaccelerated flight. What are the two erection balls doing?
options: they are balanced out, so no momentum acts on the gyro axis
they are held at their stops by the gyro cut-out rocker
they are driven apart, so a momentum acts on the gyro axis
questions.explain: With the axis in earth vertical the balls are balanced and no momentum acts on the gyro axis.

questions.question: The roll level switch of an electrically driven gyro detects the axis in an incorrect direction. What follows?
options: the roll torque motor applies a force and precession corrects it
the roll cutout switch opens and the erection circuit is broken
the caging mechanism locks the gimbals in a normal position
questions.explain: The roll level switch activates the roll torque motor, whose force precesses the gyro back into the correct direction.

questions.question: A rate of turn gyro is held by a linear spring. What can then be said about its precession angle?
options: it is proportional to the angular velocity about the measuring axis
it falls as the angular velocity about the measuring axis rises
it is independent of the angular velocity about the measuring axis
questions.explain: A linear spring makes the precession angle proportional to the angular velocity about the measuring axis.

questions.question: The system has been in DG mode for a long time and the heading has slowly wandered. What must the crew do?
options: correct the indication with the SET HDG knob
switch briefly to the slaved mode and straight back again
wait for the synchronising annunciator to null it out
questions.explain: In DG mode nothing corrects the drift automatically, so it is set out by hand.

questions.question: An HSI shows several indications driven from different sources. Which one of them is driven by the heading system?
options: the compass rose
the course bar
the distance readout
questions.explain: The rose is the heading indication; the course bar and the distance are navigation system indications.

questions.question: The approaching minimums option is selected with the aural approaching minimums. How far above the decision height does the call-out normally come on?
options: 100 feet
80 feet
130 feet
questions.explain: With the approaching minimums aural the call-out normally comes on 80 feet above the decision height; the 100 feet figure belongs to the plus hundred call-out of the same option.

questions.question: Which alerting envelopes does the terrain alerting function compute
options: A take-off envelope and a final approach envelope
A look-up envelope and a lateral offset envelope
A caution-level envelope and a warning-level envelope
questions.explain: Two envelopes are computed, one for caution level and one for warning level.

questions.question: The terrain display relays have been energised by the alert discretes. What do the navigational displays then carry?
options: The weather radar picture as before
The conflicting ground in yellow or red
The terrain test pattern in cyan
questions.explain: Once the relays are energised the conflicting ground is painted solid yellow or solid red.

questions.question: In an I-regulator the rate of change of the output value is proportional to
options: its input value
the rate of change of its input value
the change in its output value
questions.explain: In an integral regulator it is how fast the output moves that follows the input.

questions.question: With one exception, direct inputs affecting the translatory degrees of freedom are not possible. How then is the flight path controlled?
options: Indirectly, through inputs affecting initially the rotary degrees of freedom
Directly, through inputs applied to the three translatory degrees of freedom
Indirectly, through inputs affecting initially the centre of gravity position
questions.explain: The pilot has to change attitude first and let the path follow from it.

questions.question: Which parts of the autoflight system provide the combinations of regulators used for automatic vertical flight path guidance?
options: The AP/FD pitch channel and the flight management system under ATC control
The AP/FD pitch channel and the auto-thrust system under AP/FD control
The AP/FD roll channel and the auto-thrust system under FMCS control
questions.explain: Vertical guidance comes from the pitch channel together with the thrust system under AP/FD control.

questions.question: Why are flight condition regulators called basic regulators?
options: The inner control loop uses them to achieve attitude control through flight path control
The outer control loops use them to achieve flight path control through attitude control
The outer control loops replace them whenever flight path control is required
questions.explain: They are the building blocks the outer loops drive in order to steer the flight path.

questions.question: The autopilot is disengaged after a long cruise during which auto-trim has been working. Why is there no abrupt pitch attitude change?
options: The elevator is already held by the torque limiter
The stabilizer is already resting in its neutral position
The elevator is already resting in its neutral position
questions.explain: With the standing moment carried by the stabilizer and the elevator at neutral, nothing springs back at disengagement.

questions.question: The autopilot has just been engaged and no upper mode has been selected. Which attitudes do its two channels control straight away?
options: The pitch channel the pitch attitude, the roll channel the roll attitude or heading
The pitch channel the pitch attitude, the roll channel the heading only
The pitch channel the flight path, the roll channel the roll attitude or heading
questions.explain: Each channel takes its basic mode at once, pitch attitude in pitch and roll attitude or heading in roll.

questions.question: The crew has a heading mode running and air traffic control passes a different heading. When may the selected heading be altered?
options: Only after the mode has been reselected
Only after the first heading has been captured
At any time while the mode is active
questions.explain: The selected heading may be changed at any time while heading select is running.

questions.question: Why does the autopilot have to treat interception and stabilization as two separate jobs?
options: The path is continuous, but the sensors update at two different rates
The path is in segments, and each must be caught without overshoot or offset
The path is in segments, and each one has to be flown at a different airspeed
questions.explain: Because the path is built of segments, each one has to be intercepted cleanly and then held.

questions.question: The level off mode has just been selected during a climb. What does the vertical speed controller do?
options: It reduces the actual rate by half and then holds it
It holds the altitude reached when the mode was selected
It reduces the actual rate to zero and holds zero
questions.explain: The same controller drives the rate down to nothing and then keeps it there.

questions.question: The landing controller adds a height bias to the measured radio altitude close to the ground — what does this achieve at the wheels?
options: A sink rate is still commanded once the aircraft is on the ground
A thrust increase is still commanded once the aircraft is on the ground
A pitch up is still commanded once the aircraft is on the ground
questions.explain: Because the controller thinks it is higher than it is, it keeps commanding a descent and so forces a positive touch down.

questions.question: During an approach the angle of attack becomes extreme. Which protection acts and with which thrust?
options: Alpha floor protection, with go around thrust
Overspeed protection, with idle thrust
Low speed protection, with climb thrust
questions.explain: Alpha floor protection answers an extreme angle of attack by applying go around thrust.

questions.question: An operator intends to fly in all weather conditions — which flight rules must its approval cover?
options: Visual flight rules
Instrument flight rules
Special visual flight rules
questions.explain: The approval must cover IFR flight before all weather operation can follow.

questions.question: The aircraft reaches the decision height on a CAT II approach — what applies to a manual landing?
options: It is forbidden in every case
It is compulsory in every single case
It is allowed but is not compulsory
questions.explain: CAT II minima permit a manual landing without requiring one.

questions.question: What is the advancing blade
options: The forward moving blade
The blade at the tail boom
The backward moving blade
questions.explain: The blade moving forward is the advancing blade.

questions.question: Why does raising the collective lever make the rotor produce more lift
options: The rotational speed of every blade rises, and with it the chord
The pitch angle of every blade rises, and with it the angle of attack
The plane of rotation of every blade rises, and with it the relative wind
questions.explain: More pitch means more angle of attack on every blade, so the rotor makes more lift.

questions.question: The bell cranks from the cockpit controls are traced to the swash plate while the blade control rods run from its other part. Which part do the bell cranks move?
options: Both parts together
The rotating part
The stationary part
questions.explain: Cockpit inputs arrive through the bell cranks at the stationary part, and the rotating part passes the movement on to the blades.

questions.question: Why does the advancing blade flap up
options: Its centre of gravity moves closer to the blade tip
It experiences decreased relative wind and generates less lift
It experiences increased relative wind and generates more lift
questions.explain: More relative wind means more lift, so it flaps up.

questions.question: Which cockpit control does the pilot use to hold off the drift caused by translating tendency
options: The pedals, which tilt the tail rotor thrust line
The collective lever, which lifts the main rotor disk
The cyclic stick, which tilts the main rotor disk
questions.explain: Tilting the rotor disk is a cyclic input, so the cyclic stick is the control that holds off the drift.

questions.question: Which two items are special features of the integrated cabin entertainment and service system rather than subsystems of it
options: The Cabin Lighting System and the Cabin Interphone System
The Cabin Configuration System and the ACESS Test System
The Passenger Services System and the Passenger Address System
questions.explain: The CCS and the ATS are named as the two special features added to the five subsystems.

questions.question: Which cabin functions can the crew and the passengers reach through the NICE system
options: Window-shades, galley power, audio/video and seat heating
Illumination, cabin pressure, audio/video and internet access
Illumination, window-shades, audio/video and internet access
questions.explain: Illumination, window-shades, audio/video and internet access are the cabin functions printed.
